- **Title**: gh-1449 [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1449` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +986
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T13:40:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:22:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.
- AC6 (resume): hosts persist each first-time batch as the hidden `orphan_report` custom record (CLI `_onAgentEvent` + app `AgentServiceEvents`) and seed the latch from a raw record scan at session open (CLI `_loadSession` + app `loadSession`) — helpers `orphanReportRecordData` / `orphanReportKeysFromRecords` shared from `tool_pairing.dart`.
- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/tool_pairing_test.dart test/agent/orphan_notice_loop_test.dart test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart test/compaction/compaction_test.dart test/wire/ test/session/read_custom_records_test.dart
# full gate (verified: 9915 passed, 10 skipped)
dart test --exclude-tags "integration,llm,browser-ext,perf,pty"
```

<details><summary>Coverage map</summary>

- `UT-TEXT`/`UT-ROLE`/`UT-TRANSCRIPT`/`UT-ONESHOT` + E1/E2/E5/REG-PAIRING: `test/agent/tool_pairing_test.dart`
- `IT-ONESHOT` (N requests + pairing-heal retry), `IT-RESUME` (re-seeded agent), AC2 wire-shape: `test/agent/orphan_notice_loop_test.dart`
- Record round-trip through a real JSONL session: `test/session/read_custom_records_test.dart`

</details>

# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

## Open questions
1. Carrier: system/developer block vs annotation on the previous user message? (provider support differs)
2. Persist the "reported" marker in the session JSONL, or prune the orphan from live context at the cut?

## References
- Closed #85 (pair-integrity design that introduced the note), closed #858 (no replayable history may brick a session).
- Note: in the checkout I inspected (`965f7126`), `git grep` finds no literal `originating call is no longer in context` under `lib/`, so the emitting code may live elsewhere or the text may be assembled at runtime — worth confirming before implementing.

## Machine jobs

Consider this scenario: the last user message in the rebuilt payload is the pending user input ("continue"). The note is appended to it. That's the design (annotation on the adjacent/pending user message). The ticket says: "Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn." So this matches.

But hmm — there's a subtlety: the note is appended to the *pending* user message that the user just typed. When the user's message is sent, the model sees the user text + the note. Fine.

The note is a text block appended to the last user message. In the wire view, a user message's text blocks come after results. `validateToolPairing` flags `interleavedResult` when a `tool_result` appears after other content in the same wire message. The note is text appended at the END of the last user message — so if the last user message contains result blocks followed by text (the hoisted steering case), appending text after is fine (text after results, no result after text). But wait — could the LAST user message in the rebuilt payload be one that has results AFTER text? In `_rebuild`, results are emitted directly after their assistant message, so a user message in rebuilt is either a pure text message or a hoisted steering message that comes after the results were emitted. When the wire view merges adjacent user-role items, a text user message followed by ToolResultMessages merges into blocks [text, results...]? Hmm, wait — in the wire view, `UserMessage` adds `(resultId: null)` text block, and subsequent `ToolResultMessage` adds result blocks. So the merged wire user message = [text, result...] — that's results AFTER text, which is fine for the interleavedResult check (only flags result appearing after text within... wait no).

In the repair, results are emitted directly after their calls, so `pending` is empty by the time the steering text arrives. OK.

If the last message in rebuilt is a user message, nothing follows. But if rebuilt's tail is [.., UserMessage, ...] with nothing after, fine. Actually `_lastUserMessageIndex` finds the last user message wherever it is; anything after it could be assistant messages (without calls).       # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"

          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's

          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.

## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.

- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).

# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

## Open questions
1. Carrier: system/developer block vs annotation on the previous user message? (provider support differs)
2. Persist the "reported" marker in the session JSONL, or prune the orphan from live context at the cut?

## References
- Closed #85 (pair-integrity design that introduced the note), closed #858 (no replayable history may brick a session).
- Note: in the checkout I inspected (`965f7126`), `git grep` finds no literal `originating call is no longer in context` under `lib/`, so the emitting code may live elsewhere or the text may be assembled at runtime — worth confirming before implementing.

## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.

- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).

# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

## Open questions
1. Carrier: system/developer block vs annotation on the previous user message? (provider support differs)
2. Persist the "reported" marker in the session JSONL, or prune the orphan from live context at the cut?

## References
- Closed #85 (pair-integrity design that introduced the note), closed #858 (no replayable history may brick a session).
- Note: in the checkout I inspected (`965f7126`), `git grep` finds no literal `originating call is no longer in context` under `lib/`, so the emitting code may live elsewhere or the text may be assembled at runtime — worth confirming before implementing.

So if `notedOrphanKeys` is non-empty, then `droppedResultIds` is non-empty. So `isNotEmpty` doesn't need updating. OK, fine.

**Issue 2: Note rides LAST user message — could be a STEERING message that gets... wait**, the last user message in `rebuilt`. Consider this scenario: the last user message in the rebuilt payload is the pending user input ("continue"). The note is appended to it. That's the design (annotation on the adjacent/pending user message). The ticket says: "Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn." So this matches.

But hmm — there's a subtlety: the note is appended to the *pending* user message that the user just typed. When the user's message is sent, the model sees the user text + the note. Fine.

**Issue 3 (potential correctness): the carrier promotion and `validateToolPairing` after the note append.** After appending the note to the last user message, could the repaired payload become INVALID again? The note is a text block appended to the last user message. In the wire view, a user message's text blocks come after results. `validateToolPairing` flags `interleavedResult` when a `tool_result` appears after other content in the same wire message. The note is text appended at the END of the last user message — so if the last user message contains result blocks followed by text (the hoisted steering case), appending text after is fine (text after results, no result after text). But wait — could the LAST user message in the rebuilt payload be one that has results AFTER text? In `_rebuild`, results are emitted directly after their assistant message, so a user message in rebuilt is either a pure text message or a hoisted steering message that comes after the results were emitted. When the wire view merges adjacent user-role items, a text user message followed by ToolResultMessages merges into blocks [text, results...]? Hmm, wait — in the wire view, `UserMessage` adds `(resultId: null)` text block, and subsequent `ToolResultMessage` adds result blocks. So the merged wire user message = [text, result...] — that's results AFTER text, which is fine for the interleavedResult check (only flags result appearing after text within... wait no).

Let me re-read `validateToolPairing`: for `_WireUser` blocks: `sawText` is set when a text block is seen; a result block AFTER text sets `interleavedResult`... but only if the result id is in `pending` (i.e. unanswered call from the previous assistant message). In the repair, results are emitted directly after their calls, so `pending` is empty by the time the steering text arrives. OK.

Now the note append: `rebuilt[carrierIndex]` is the last UserMessage in rebuilt. Since it's the last user message and comes after everything, appending a text block cannot create a result-after-text within its merged wire group. But could there be ToolResultMessages AFTER the carrier user message in rebuilt? No — it's the LAST user message index; anything after it in rebuilt could only be... ToolResultMessages are emitted right after their assistant calls. Could there be a ToolResultMessage after the last user message? Results are emitted immediately after the assistant message. If the last message in rebuilt is a user message, nothing follows. But if rebuilt's tail is [.., UserMessage, ...] with nothing after, fine. Actually `_lastUserMessageIndex` finds the last user message wherever it is; anything after it could be assistant messages (without calls). Appending a note to a user message that is followed by assistant messages — fine for wire validity.

Edge: a UserMessage whose content is an empty string? `_withAppendedNote` on empty-string content: blocks = [TextContent(text: '')], note]. Probably harmless for providers? Actually the Anthropic adapter `_convertUserMessage` filters empty text blocks? The `_userVisible` helper says adapters skip whitespace-only user text — as a whole message. A message with an empty text block + note text block: the note block is non-empty so the message is visible. OK.

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). ### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).

blocks.text:
# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

So if `notedOrphanKeys` is non-empty, then `droppedResultIds` is non-empty. So `isNotEmpty` doesn't need updating. OK, fine.

**Issue 2: Note rides LAST user message — could be a STEERING message that gets... wait**, the last user message in `rebuilt`. Consider this scenario: the last user message in the rebuilt payload is the pending user input ("continue"). The note is appended to it. That's the design (annotation on the adjacent/pending user message). The ticket says: "Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn." So this matches.

But hmm — there's a subtlety: the note is appended to the *pending* user message that the user just typed. When the user's message is sent, the model sees the user text + the note. Fine.

**Issue 3 (potential correctness): the carrier promotion and `validateToolPairing` after the note append.** After appending the note to the last user message, could the repaired payload become INVALID again? The note is a text block appended to the last user message. In the wire view, a user message's text blocks come after results. `validateToolPairing` flags `interleavedResult` when a `tool_result` appears after other content in the same wire message. The note is text appended at the END of the last user message — so if the last user message contains result blocks followed by text (the hoisted steering case), appending text after is fine (text after results, no result after text). But wait — could the LAST user message in the rebuilt payload be one that has results AFTER text? In `_rebuild`, results are emitted directly after their assistant message, so a user message in rebuilt is either a pure text message or a hoisted steering message that comes after the results were emitted. When the wire view merges adjacent user-role items, a text user message followed by ToolResultMessages merges into blocks [text, results...]? Hmm, wait — in the wire view, `UserMessage` adds `(resultId: null)` text block, and subsequent `ToolResultMessage` adds result blocks. So the merged wire user message = [text, result...] — that's results AFTER text, which is fine for the interleavedResult check (only flags result appearing after text within... wait no).

Let me re-read `validateToolPairing`: for `_WireUser` blocks: `sawText` is set when a text block is seen; a result block AFTER text sets `interleavedResult`... but only if the result id is in `pending` (i.e. unanswered call from the previous assistant message). In the repair, results are emitted directly after their calls, so `pending` is empty by the time the steering text arrives. OK.

Now the note append: `rebuilt[carrierIndex]` is the last UserMessage in rebuilt. Since it's the last user message and comes after everything, appending a text block cannot create a result-after-text within its merged wire group. Actually `_lastUserMessageIndex` finds the last user message wherever it is; anything after it could be assistant messages (without calls). Appending a note to a user message that is followed by assistant messages — fine for wire validity.

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. - **PR #**: 1451
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1451
- **Title**: gh-1449 [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1449` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +986
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T13:40:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:22:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.
- AC6 (resume): hosts persist each first-time batch as the hidden `orphan_report` custom record (CLI `_onAgentEvent` + app `AgentServiceEvents`) and seed the latch from a raw record scan at session open (CLI `_loadSession` + app `loadSession`) — helpers `orphanReportRecordData` / `orphanReportKeysFromRecords` shared from `tool_pairing.dart`.
- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/tool_pairing_test.dart test/agent/orphan_notice_loop_test.dart test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart test/compaction/compaction_test.dart test/wire/ test/session/read_custom_records_test.dart
# full gate (verified: 9915 passed, 10 skipped)
dart test --exclude-tags "integration,llm,browser-ext,perf,pty"
```

<details><summary>Coverage map</summary>

- `UT-TEXT`/`UT-ROLE`/`UT-TRANSCRIPT`/`UT-ONESHOT` + E1/E2/E5/REG-PAIRING: `test/agent/tool_pairing_test.dart`
- `IT-ONESHOT` (N requests + pairing-heal retry), `IT-RESUME` (re-seeded agent), AC2 wire-shape: `test/agent/orphan_notice_loop_test.dart`
- Record round-trip through a real JSONL session: `test/session/read_custom_records_test.dart`

</details>

# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

## Open questions
1. Carrier: system/developer block vs annotation on the previous user message? (provider support differs)
2. Persist the "reported" marker in the session JSONL, or prune the orphan from live context at the cut?

## References
- Closed #85 (pair-integrity design that introduced the note), closed #858 (no replayable history may brick a session).
- Note: in the checkout I inspected (`965f7126`), `git grep` finds no literal `originating call is no longer in context` under `lib/`, so the emitting code may live elsewhere or the text may be assembled at runtime — worth confirming before implementing.

Now I have the full `tool_pairing.dart`. Let me analyze for issues:

**Issue 1: `isNotEmpty` doesn't include `notedOrphanKeys`** — Actually, `notedOrphanKeys` is a subset of `droppedResultIds`... wait, is it? `notedOrphanKeys` contains keys for `freshOrphans` (subset of orphans). `droppedResultIds` includes ALL orphans. So if `notedOrphanKeys` is non-empty, then `droppedResultIds` is non-empty. So `isNotEmpty` doesn't need updating. OK, fine.

**Issue 2: Note rides LAST user message — could be a STEERING message that gets... wait**, the last user message in `rebuilt`. Consider this scenario: the last user message in the rebuilt payload is the pending user input ("continue"). The note is appended to it. That's the design (annotation on the adjacent/pending user message). The ticket says: "Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn." So this matches.

But hmm — there's a subtlety: the note is appended to the *pending* user message that the user just typed. When the user's message is sent, the model sees the user text + the note. Fine.

**Issue 3 (potential correctness): the carrier promotion and `validateToolPairing` after the note append.** After appending the note to the last user message, could the repaired payload become INVALID again? The note is a text block appended to the last user message. In the wire view, a user message's text blocks come after results. `validateToolPairing` flags `interleavedResult` when a `tool_result` appears after other content in the same wire message. The note is text appended at the END of the last user message — so if the last user message contains result blocks followed by text (the hoisted steering case), appending text after is fine (text after results, no result after text). But wait — could the LAST user message in the rebuilt payload be one that has results AFTER text? In `_rebuild`, results are emitted directly after their assistant message, so a user message in rebuilt is either a pure text message or a hoisted steering message that comes after the results were emitted. When the wire view merges adjacent user-role items, a text user message followed by ToolResultMessages merges into blocks [text, results...]? Hmm, wait — in the wire view, `UserMessage` adds `(resultId: null)` text block, and subsequent `ToolResultMessage` adds result blocks. So the merged wire user message = [text, result...] — that's results AFTER text, which is fine for the interleavedResult check (only flags result appearing after text within... wait no).

Let me re-read `validateToolPairing`: for `_WireUser` blocks: `sawText` is set when a text block is seen; a result block AFTER text sets `interleavedResult`... but only if the result id is in `pending` (i.e. unanswered call from the previous assistant message). In the repair, results are emitted directly after their calls, so `pending` is empty by the time the steering text arrives. OK.

Now the note append: `rebuilt[carrierIndex]` is the last UserMessage in rebuilt. Since it's the last user message and comes after everything, appending a text block cannot create a result-after-text within its merged wire group. But could there be ToolResultMessages AFTER the carrier user message in rebuilt? No — it's the LAST user message index; anything after it in rebuilt could only be... ToolResultMessages are emitted right after their assistant calls. Could there be a ToolResultMessage after the last user message? Results are emitted immediately after the assistant message. If the last message in rebuilt is a user message, nothing follows. But if rebuilt's tail is [.., UserMessage, ...] with nothing after, fine. Actually `_lastUserMessageIndex` finds the last user message wherever it is; anything after it could be assistant messages (without calls). Appending a note to a user message that is followed by assistant messages — fine for wire validity.

Edge: a UserMessage whose content is an empty string? `_withAppendedNote` on empty-string content: blocks = [TextContent(text: '')], note]. Text block with empty text — `_userVisible` returns false for empty text... but that's for validation of original messages. The carrier would produce a wire text block with empty text plus the note. Probably harmless for providers? Actually the Anthropic adapter `_convertUserMessage` filters empty text blocks? The `_userVisible` helper says adapters skip whitespace-only user text — as a whole message. A message with an empty text block + note text block: the note block is non-empty so the message is visible. OK.

**Issue 4: `_withAppendedNote` drops non-String, non-List content silently** (`...const <ContentBlock>[]`). UserMessage content type — is it `String` or `List<ContentBlock>`? Let me check types.dart. If content can only be those two, the else branch is dead defensive code. Minor.

**Issue 5: E1 key stability across resume — timestamp round-trip.** The key is `canonicalToolCallId|toolName|timestampMs`. Does the transcript persist the timestamp exactly? `millisecondsSinceEpoch` — if the session JSONL stores ISO8601 with microsecond precision, round-trip should be exact. But what about timezone? DateTime is UTC-based ms since epoch — fine. But what about the resume path: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — does it rebuild messages with different timestamps? Let me check. Also, do messages loaded from session have timestamps reconstructed exactly? Need to check `session_record.dart` / message serialization.

Also the note in the transcript: the ORPHAN RESULT remains in the transcript forever (transcript untouched). On each new request, it's still an orphan and dropped. The latch grows unbounded across session — minor.

**Issue 6: Latch key collision** — `canonicalToolCallId` truncates to 40 chars. Two different ids truncating to the same 40-char canonical + same tool + same ms timestamp → collision. Negligible.

**Issue 7 (IMPORTANT): the wire encode `'notedOrphanKeys': ?report.notedOrphanKeys.isEmpty ? null : ...`** — the `?` null-aware element syntax; fine in modern Dart. Decode: `key as String` — if a peer sends non-string keys → cast error → frame decode fails. Legacy protocol tolerance: decode of `notedOrphanKeys` assumes list of strings; a malicious/corrupt peer could crash. Minor robustness; other fields in the same decoder probably do the same (e.g. droppedResultIds `as String`). Consistent with existing code, fine.

**Issue 8 (IMPORTANT?): `_dropNote` single-orphan line is long** — style only.

**Issue 9: `_orphanNoteClause` `kept` probe — substring scan of the boundary text for the canonical call id.** The call id like `bash_1` could appear in the summary as part of another id e.g. `bash_12` → false positive "kept in summary: yes". Minor/acceptable heuristic, documented.

**Issue 10: `_nearestCutBoundary` requires `content is String`** — after the FIRST repair appends the note to a carrier, the carrier content becomes a List<ContentBlock>! On the NEXT request, the payload is rebuilt from the transcript (original), so this is fine for the loop path. But when repair is invoked on an already-repaired payload (e.g. `auto_compactor._localTrimFallback` routes kept region through repairer — payload built from state.messages which are transcript messages, not repaired ones). Hmm, but wait: `_noteCount` in tests uses `userMessageText`. The boundary probe only checks `content is String` — if the compaction summary user message in the payload has block content (List<ContentBlock>), the boundary is not detected → label 'context cut'. When could a compaction summary be a block-content user message? Compaction creates UserMessage.text presumably. Fine, but the miss case degrades gracefully to 'context cut'. OK.

## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.

- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).

# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

## Open questions
1. Carrier: system/developer block vs annotation on the previous user message? (provider support differs)
2. Persist the "reported" marker in the session JSONL, or prune the orphan from live context at the cut?

## References
- Closed #85 (pair-integrity design that introduced the note), closed #858 (no replayable history may brick a session).
- Note: in the checkout I inspected (`965f7126`), `git grep` finds no literal `originating call is no longer in context` under `lib/`, so the emitting code may live elsewhere or the text may be assembled at runtime — worth confirming before implementing.

Consider this scenario: the last user message in the rebuilt payload is the pending user input ("continue"). The note is appended to it. That's the design (annotation on the adjacent/pending user message). The ticket says: "Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn." So this matches.

But hmm — there's a subtlety: the note is appended to the *pending* user message that the user just typed. When the user's message is sent, the model sees the user text + the note. Fine.

The note is a text block appended to the last user message. In the wire view, a user message's text blocks come after results. `validateToolPairing` flags `interleavedResult` when a `tool_result` appears after other content in the same wire message. The note is text appended at the END of the last user message — so if the last user message contains result blocks followed by text (the hoisted steering case), appending text after is fine (text after results, no result after text). But wait — could the LAST user message in the rebuilt payload be one that has results AFTER text? In `_rebuild`, results are emitted directly after their assistant message, so a user message in rebuilt is either a pure text message or a hoisted steering message that comes after the results were emitted. When the wire view merges adjacent user-role items, a text user message followed by ToolResultMessages merges into blocks [text, results...]? In the repair, results are emitted directly after their calls, so `pending` is empty by the time the steering text arrives. OK.

ToolResultMessages are emitted right after their assistant calls. Could there be a ToolResultMessage after the last user message? Results are emitted immediately after the assistant message. If the last message in rebuilt is a user message, nothing follows. But if rebuilt's tail is [.., UserMessage, ...] with nothing after, fine. Actually `_lastUserMessageIndex` finds the last user message wherever it is; anything after it could be assistant messages (without calls). Appending a note to a user message that is followed by assistant messages — fine for wire validity.

# Pull Request Information

- **Title**: gh-1449 [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1449` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +986
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T13:40:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T14:22:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.
- AC6 (resume): hosts persist each first-time batch as the hidden `orphan_report` custom record (CLI `_onAgentEvent` + app `AgentServiceEvents`) and seed the latch from a raw record scan at session open (CLI `_loadSession` + app `loadSession`) — helpers `orphanReportRecordData` / `orphanReportKeysFromRecords` shared from `tool_pairing.dart`.
- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).

### How to verify

# gh-1449: [GOAL] Orphan-result notices: reported once, never a user turn, always identifies the call

## Description

## Goal — orphan-result notices (v1)

One sentence: **a dropped-orphan tool result is repaired silently at the request boundary — the notice never costs the model a turn, never repeats, and always says which call it concerns.**

Observed in a long orchestration session (dmtools work, ~15 sub-agents via `task`, many context compactions): the model repeatedly received a message of the form `[context note: a tool result for "task" (id: toolu_…) was dropped — its originating call is no longer in context]` and answered it each time ("this is an old sub-agent call, results already handled"). It arrived 10+ times in one session. `task_status` showed every sub-agent `completed`, so nothing was actually lost; the model could not tell which call it concerned and had to guess.

## Why this framing
- The note template comes from the pair-integrity design (closed #85): drop an orphan `tool_result`, replace it with a one-line user-role note "so the model isn't gaslit about missing work". That repair is correct. The **delivery** is the problem: a user-role note is indistinguishable from a user turn, so it triggers a reply, and it is regenerated whenever the same orphan is still in the transcript.
- Retracted framing: "the model should explain what was dropped". The model cannot know — the originating call is gone by definition. An explanation is always a guess.

## Architecture
- Component: the request-boundary pairing repair (`lib/src/agent/`, runs after `transformContext`, before `streamFunction` — the place `repairOrphanedToolCalls` already runs).
- Invariants:
  1. **One-shot per orphan.** An orphan is reported once per session; the transcript records that it was reported (or the repair removes the orphan from the live context permanently), so the next request does not re-emit the note.
  2. **Not a turn.** The notice is carried as non-conversational context (system/developer-role block or annotation on the adjacent message), never as a new user-role message that invites a reply. Providers that only accept user/assistant roles get it appended to the existing preceding user message, not as its own turn.
  3. **Identifiable.** The note names the tool, the tool-call id, the compaction/cut that removed the call and whether a result summary survives (`kept in summary: yes/no`).
  4. **No transcript rewrite.** Same rule as the existing repairer: outbound only.
- Fallback: if role/placement cannot be honoured for a provider, keep today's behaviour but log a visible `repair` event (silent context surgery is how #85 happened).

## Capability surface
| Subject | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan `tool_result` in outbound context | dropped + note | dropped, reported once |
| The note | user-role message, regenerated | non-turn carrier, one-shot, names call/id/cut |
| Transcript | untouched | untouched (+ a small "orphan reported" marker, or the orphan pruned from live context) |
| Compaction cut points | may leave results whose call was cut | audited: no cut leaves an orphan unless reported once |

Tiers — core: one-shot + non-turn carrier + identifiable text. Second tier: `kept in summary` hint, a TUI/CLI line showing the repair. Excluded (with rationale): asking the model to re-run the lost call — the repair cannot know it is still needed; auto-restoring the call — would rewrite history.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — A context with one orphan result produces exactly one note across N consecutive requests (test `IT-ONESHOT`).
- **AC2** — The note is never delivered as a stand-alone user-role message (test `UT-ROLE`, per provider adapter).
- **AC3** — The note contains tool name, call id and the cut reference (test `UT-TEXT`).
- **AC4** — Transcript bytes are identical before/after the repair (`UT-TRANSCRIPT`).
- **AC5** — Existing pairing behaviour of #85 is unchanged: orphan call → synthetic interrupted result; duplicate ids → uniquified (`REG-PAIRING`).
- **AC6** — A resumed/restored session that already reported an orphan does not report it again (`IT-RESUME`).

## Test plan
- `UT-ROLE`, `UT-TEXT`, `UT-TRANSCRIPT` — pure, per provider adapter (Anthropic, OpenAI chat/responses, Gemini).
- `IT-ONESHOT`, `IT-RESUME` — fake provider, deterministic clock, session with a compaction cut that orphans a result.
- `E2E-LONG` — long scripted session with repeated compactions and sub-agent (`task`) calls: count of model turns whose only input is a repair note must be 0.
- `REG-PAIRING` — all existing #85/#858 pairing tests through the new path; a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

## Edge cases
- **E1** — orphan result whose call id is reused by a later run (ids reset per run): report once per (id, position).
- **E2** — two orphans in one request: one combined note, both named.
- **E3** — note arrives while the user is typing / a turn is already queued: must not wake an idle session.
- **E4** — headless/CI session (no TUI): the repair is still logged.
- **E5** — provider rejects the carrier role: degrade to the current behaviour + event.

## Non-goals
- Changing what compaction keeps. No new UI. No change to #85 pairing semantics.

## Open questions
1. Carrier: system/developer block vs annotation on the previous user message? (provider support differs)
2. Persist the "reported" marker in the session JSONL, or prune the orphan from live context at the cut?

## References
- Closed #85 (pair-integrity design that introduced the note), closed #858 (no replayable history may brick a session).
- Note: in the checkout I inspected (`965f7126`), `git grep` finds no literal `originating call is no longer in context` under `lib/`, so the emitting code may live elsewhere or the text may be assembled at runtime — worth confirming before implementing.

The note is text appended at the END of the last user message — so if the last user message contains result blocks followed by text (the hoisted steering case), appending text after is fine (text after results, no result after text). But wait — could the LAST user message in the rebuilt payload be one that has results AFTER text? Now the note append: `rebuilt[carrierIndex]` is the last UserMessage in rebuilt. Since it's the last user message and comes after everything, appending a text block cannot create a result-after-text within its merged wire group. If the last message in rebuilt is a user message, nothing follows. But if rebuilt's tail is [.., UserMessage, ...] with nothing after, fine. ## PR Description

Closes #1449
### What changed

Orphan-result drop notes (issue gh-1449) are now **one-shot and never a user turn**: the repairer drops the orphan from the payload and reports it exactly once per session, annotating the payload's LAST existing user message with an extra text block instead of appending a new user message at the end (which the model answered, every time). The note names the tool, call id, the cut that removed the call (`compaction summary` / `branch summary` / `local trim` / `context marker`), and a `kept in summary: yes|no` hint, and ends with "No reply needed."

### Key decisions

- One-shot latch = stable key `canonicalToolCallId|tool|timestampMs` (`orphanReportKey`) — ids reset per run, so the timestamp is the position discriminator (E1: same id reused later reports again; the same orphan never does).
- Latch state lives on `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys` (seedable via constructor), threaded through `AgentLoopConfig`; the loop merges `report.notedOrphanKeys` back so retries (incl. the pairing-heal retry) see them.

- Transcript stays untouched (payload-only, `UT-TRANSCRIPT`); degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone note (no carrier exists); wire frame gains optional `notedOrphanKeys` (backward-compatible, golden pinned).
